assessment: Two narrow tutors, one per kind of missing piece. Idyllic Tutor ({2}{W}, sorcery) finds an enchantment, and the 99 holds eight: Artist's Talent, Fiery Emancipation, Gratuitous Violence, Knowledge Is Power, Rhystic Study, Smothering Tithe, Sorcerer Class, Teferi's Ageless Insight. Stoneforge Mystic ({1}{W}) finds one of nine Equipment: Brotherhood Regalia, Champion's Helm, Embercleave, Fireshrieker, Genji Glove, Lightning Greaves, Lizard Blades, Mask of Memory, Zephyr Boots. She can also put an Equipment from your hand onto the battlefield for {1}{W}, which skips its casting cost. Both cost white, the thinnest colour: 19 land sources against a target of 22. Neither finds a commander, a wheel or a shield spell, so neither replaces a keep. The default for each is the piece that closes on the board you have; every damage figure below that goes past stacks 001, 004 and 005 is oracle arithmetic and needs a stack scenario.

targets.scenario: A commander is out and has survived a turn cycle, you hold a double-strike piece or Blade Historian is on the battlefield, and you have no damage multiplier.
targets.why: It doubles damage from any creature you control, so it serves both commanders: Shabraz's swing and Brallin's swing and pings. By oracle arithmetic a 10/10 with double strike under it is 40 to one seat, where the same hit without it is 20. Five mana on the turn after the tutor. Needs a stack scenario: no passing stack resolves combat in this deck.

targets.scenario: Shabraz is out, a wheel is in hand, and you are one turn from swinging with nothing that adds to his size beyond his own counters.
targets.why: Every creature gets +X/+X, X being the cards you drew this turn, so the wheel turn is also the pump turn. Stack 001 leaves Shabraz a 10/10 after Windfall, and double strike on that is 20, one short; this is the card that covers the gap. It costs {3}{W}{U}, so plan Idyllic one turn and Knowledge Is Power plus the wheel the next. The +X arithmetic needs a stack scenario.

targets.scenario: Turn three or four, no commander resolved yet, a symmetrical wheel (Windfall, Reforge the Soul, Jace's Archivist) in hand, and ramp short: the game 001 problem.
targets.why: Each opponent draw is a Treasure unless that player pays {2}, and a symmetrical wheel makes every opponent draw seven at once. That is the mana for a commander plus an equip on the same turn. Tithe must be on the battlefield before the wheel. It is a Game Changer and it taxes the whole table, so it draws attention; the payment the table chooses is not modelled anywhere. Oracle text only.

targets.scenario: Brallin is out, Torbran or a level-3 Artist's Talent is not, and the table is at life totals a seven-card wheel cannot reach from pings alone.
targets.why: The one nobody sees. It triples damage from any source you control, Brallin's pings included, so by oracle arithmetic seven discards would be 21 to each opponent: the figure stacks 004 and 005 reach with other cards. It also triples either commander's swing. Six mana with {R}{R}{R}, so it is a two-turn plan. Needs a stack scenario.

tutors.notes: A three-mana sorcery that does nothing to the board the turn you cast it. Cast it on a quiet turn, never on the turn you intend to swing.

targets.scenario: Turn two or three, no commander yet, no protection in hand, and the table has removal up.
targets.why: Haste and shroud, equip {0}: the commander lands and can swing the turn it arrives, and opponents cannot target it. Shroud stops your own targeting too, so move Greaves to another creature before you attach anything else. Brallin was removed twice in game 001.

citations.quote: Shroud is a static ability. “Shroud” means “This permanent or player can’t be the target of spells or abilities.”

targets.scenario: A commander with counters is out without Greaves on it, Stoneforge has been on the battlefield since your turn began, and {1}{W} is open.
targets.why: The closer. Stoneforge puts it onto the battlefield for {1}{W} instead of {4}{R}{R}, and its enters trigger attaches it to target creature you control: double strike, trample and +1/+1. Her ability has no timing restriction, so you can do it after blockers are declared. She taps to do it, so not on the turn she arrives. The trigger targets, so it cannot attach to a Greaves-wearing commander.

citations.quote: A player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority.

A creature’s activated ability with the tap symbol or the untap symbol in its activation cost can’t be activated unless the creature has been under its controller’s control continuously since their most recent turn began.

targets.scenario: Brallin is the commander you are swinging with, the defender has ground blockers, and you have no evasion piece.
targets.why: Can't be blocked and ward {2}, and equip legendary creature is {1}, so it goes on either commander for one mana. Shabraz already flies; Brallin does not, and Regalia is the one fetch that gives him both evasion and protection. Pair it with a double-strike piece already in hand.

targets.scenario: One opponent is near 21 commander damage from a grown commander, a second seat is also low, and you hold no double-strike piece.
targets.why: Double strike plus an extra combat phase, and Stoneforge puts it in without paying {5}; equip is still {3}. Each combat lets you attack a different seat, so it is the fetch that can take two opponents in one turn. Whether that line kills two seats needs a stack scenario.

tutors.notes: She finds Equipment only. Equip costs still apply to everything except Embercleave's own attach trigger, so count the equip mana before you choose the target.

gaps: No passing stack resolves combat in this deck, so every commander-damage figure here past stacks 001, 004 and 005 is oracle arithmetic.
The goldfish declares no group for either tutor's targets, so how often a tutor finds its piece in time is unpriced.
Smothering Tithe's yield depends on how often opponents pay {2}; no figure for this table exists.
Brallin's partner trigger puts Shabraz into a hand 'from their library'. It is not a library search, and Shabraz starts in the command zone, so it is not covered here.
